Synopsis:
 The Trump administration defends a deal granting US-backed entity Nabep 100-year rights over 17 Venezuelan oil fields (covering ~65bn barrels), framed as stabilising Venezuela post-Maduro while securing US strategic crude access. The deal is set against a backdrop of soaring US fuel prices (~$4.10/gal) following a US-Iran war that closed the Strait of Hormuz. Opposition to the deal is significant domestically in Venezuela. The Energy Secretary is travelling to Caracas to advance implementation. Long-term democratic transition remains uncertain.
